decisions.reason: The passenger data transmission solution sits close to the firm's core aviation security know-how and has strong quantified evidence: it is used by the UK Home Office and connected to over 30 government APIS schemes, so the firm can interpret its results and keep improving it.

The travel health requirements API builds on the firm's passenger data and document expertise and has its own page, but demand for post-pandemic health rules is fading and no results are reported, so its value is uncertain even though it can likely be folded into the related platforms.

The cyber security awareness module fits the firm's certified-trainer and training capabilities, so it builds on existing knowledge at low cost, although it is only mentioned on the website and shows no reported results.

The behaviour analysis system extends the firm's established behavioural detection expertise, which gives it the related knowledge to assimilate feedback and refine the product, despite limited visibility on the website.
The passenger profiling method draws directly on the firm's core aviation screening knowledge and operational know-how, making it a natural extension the firm can learn from and improve.

The travel and document verification platform is close to the firm's established document-check offer for airlines and has its own page, so it complements Product A and the firm can readily interpret and apply its market results.
